chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Durays ibn Abd al-Malik, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man makes the private part of his slave-girl permissible for his brother. He said: It is lawful for him. I said: If she bears a child from him? He said: The child belongs to the master of the slave-girl, unless he stipulated with the master of the slave-girl when he made her permissible for him: If she bears a child, he is free.
ai.seo_question: Who owns the child born from a slave-girl made permissible for another man?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar elucidates the fiqh of 'tahlil' (temporary marriage/permissibility) regarding slave-girls, establishing that the child's lineage and status default to the master unless a specific condition of emancipation was stipulated at the time of the arrangement. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on contractual conditions in determining the legal status of offspring in slave-holding contexts, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams. The ruling underscores the flexibility of private agreements in modifying default legal outcomes within the framework of slavery.
